candidates.exact_span: The State of New Mexico and Navajo Nation WQS criteria applicable to the warm-water aquatic life designated use are at least 5 mg/L and 6 mg/L, respectively, for dissolved oxygen.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of which receiving-water DO criterion applies (5 mg/L vs 6 mg/L, or both) could change which numeric standard is treated as the basis for applicable discharge or receiving-water limits and compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: to develop permit parameters for the protection of the State of New Mexico surface water WQS for DO (i.e., 5 mg/L).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this passage is read as selecting only the New Mexico 5 mg/L DO criterion for permit limit derivation, as opposed to the Navajo Nation 6 mg/L criterion also mentioned, could change which enforceable numeric limit is deemed applicable.

candidates.exact_span: various BOD5 factors including BOD5 Secondary Treatment Standards were considered and simulated to achieve the DO criterion.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpreting this as tying effluent BOD5 limits to Secondary Treatment Standards versus site-specific modeled limits could change which enforceable numeric BOD5 limits are treated as applicable.

candidates.exact_span: The model results show no excursion of the receiving stream DO standard of 6 mg/L when the BOD5 limits of 30 mg/l for monthly average and 45 mg/l for 7-day maxima were applied (see graph with 30/45 mg/L BOD5 in Appendix 1; other detail information is available upon request).
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage states numeric BOD5 limits and averaging periods (monthly average, 7-day maxima) and references a 6 mg/L receiving-stream DO standard; different interpretations of whether these values are operative permit limits, which averaging period governs each measurement, and which DO standard controls could change limit-applicability computations (A) and monitoring-period obligation evaluations (B).

candidates.exact_span: Other effluent parameters provided in the permittee’s application and applied in the model include Ammonia (Avg: 8 mg/L), DO (Avg: 5.63 mg/L), temperature (23 C), Nitrate plus Nitrite Nitrogen (Avg: 20 mg/L), T. Phosphorus (2.9 mg/L) and E. Coli (Avg: 4 MPN/100 mL).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether these application values are treated as modeled inputs only or as stated effluent concentrations that imply applicable numeric limits for ammonia, DO, nitrogen, phosphorus, and E. coli could change which parameters receive enforceable limit comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: The discharge location provided in the permit application is located at Latitude 36° 43' 02" N (36.7172), and Longitude 108° 13' 15" W (-108.2208).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different interpretations of discharge-point location could change which jurisdictional water-quality criteria (State of New Mexico versus Navajo Nation) are deemed applicable to limits at that outfall.

candidates.exact_span: A complete characterization of San Juan River (i.e., water quality and hydrodynamic data) was not available. Where data were not available, estimates and assumptions are made.
candidates.computation_change_reason: How this missing-data statement is classified—as documented absence of basis data, assumed substitute values, or unresolved uncertainty—could change missing-evidence semantics (C) and whether limit or monitoring applicability can be established versus left unresolved (A, B).

candidates.exact_span: receiving stream average depth of 6 feet (2 meters) were assumed since no data available.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This documents a no-data state filled by assumption; interpreting it as a documented modeling assumption versus evidence of missing required characterization could change how absent ordinary numeric results or supporting data are categorized.

candidates.exact_span: Should these conditions change, the model should be updated to provide a more accurate assessment of the water quality within the receiving water body.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this is read as a conditional trigger for revised limits or reassessment when design flow, critical flow, or other modeled conditions change could affect determinations of when monitoring or limit re-evaluation obligations apply (B) and when prior limit applicability remains valid versus becomes unresolved (A, C).
